questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Having a varied choice of film classes

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Southampton was super helpful and accomadating upon arrival

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved help switching classses, tours around campus from older students and preliminary understanding of the university as a whole from the academic skills for international students class

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Various locations depending on which campus I would be spending most time on, various room types depending on different types

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a meal plan that I did not use, my flat had a fully working kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you are a very cleanly person and you get placed with people who are not the shared kitchen can be a little challenging

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The majority of the process was form based and through email

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Pretty quick email correspondence

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful as all the classes I wanted were filled up. Not sure if international students are given access to class resigtration after home students or if the classes I picked were just super popular. Luckily I could find others I found interesting and I had lots of help with dropping and switching the classes I did not end up enjoying once I arrived.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to not get your first choice of classes or accommodation

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was a third (final) year BA student and I took classes mainly with other third year students and one with second years. Both levels were somewhat similar to what I had expected and were not hard to keep up with

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Somewhat similar to Copenhagen but slightly less structured seminars

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Music in Film and Television, Television Studies, Narrative Non-Fiction writing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would reccomend all three, they were super interesting and engaging. The professors were all super kind and helpful

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Only that kitchen supplies were not shared amougst flatmates and each individual required thingss such as pots, pans, dishware and cutlery I was a little surprised rent was paid quarterly instead of monthly but that was noted in my accommodation rent agreement so it was not surprising while I was abroad.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was cheaper both from the supermarket and at restaurants

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many societies were available but I did not join any. There were sports related ones, academic focused ones, craft societies, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visiting surrounding cities and going to the movies, both are fun aways to experience the difference in culture

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Brighton, London, more Northern cities. Make plans with friends outside of academic settings, there are a lot of nice outdoor places in Southampton.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try and talk to them in class, I had some people approach me and ask to go see a movie and once we were in a social setting it was easy to get to know them. Talking to your flatmates is another way

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really, there was much more vaping in the UK than Denmark and that bothered me a bit

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pub culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to be flexible, use your your professors as much as possible and spend time getting to know the other international students

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic aspects, I really enjoyed studying something new and learning a whole new set of tools needed for that

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Spending so much time alone in the start and adjusting to a new routine

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
